1. Executive Summary
 
3
 
•Phase 1 capital request: $350,000 over a 12-month program period, based in California.•Average monthly operating burn: $29,167. Committed spend $325,639; contingency reserve $24,361 
(7.0%).
•Provisional patent filed June 15, 2026; utility conversion funded within this program.•Two founders, combining systems engineering and production manufacturing operations.•Initial $10,000 tranche committed (FlexAI / Platinum Eagle Aerospace), deploying on a defined 45-day 
schedule (Section 11).
•Zero institutional capital raised to date.
ScanIQis a closed-loop manufacturing intelligence platform. Our system scans a physical part, reconstructs it 
as a continuous geometric field, produces machine-ready toolpaths, and then measures the finished result using sensors already installed on modern production machines. Every dimensional error measured is fed back into the next iteration, so the system converges on true dimension instead of repeating the same mistake indefinitely.Conventional manufacturing software is open-loop. A slicer or CAM package generates a toolpath and never learns what the machine actually produced. Dimensional accuracy therefore depends on operator skill and manual calibration. In our own bench testing, uncorrected machine drift produced parts measuring between 199.2 mm and 206.5 mm against a 200 mm target. Following closed-loop correction, a calibrated iteration measured within 0.03 mm of target.The company is founder-funded to date, with a provisional patent filed on June 15, 2026, a live platform at scaniq.live, and active pilot relationships in the motocross and performance suspension market. We are seeking $350,000 to fund a 12-month California program (Phase 1) that validates the platform in a beachhead market and expands into aerospace and maritime legacy-component replication. A follow-on Phase 2 program, outlined in Section 13, extends operations into Montana for agricultural research and manufacturing.This capital is intended to be leveraged, not consumed. The 18-month program is structured to position the company for non-dilutive federal awards — NSF, USDA, and Department of Defense SBIR programs — that together represent substantially more capital than this raise, without further dilution.
Key Facts

3. The Problem
 
2. Company Overview
 
4
 
Production machines deviate from nominal dimension due to thermal behavior, material variation, mechanical wear, and calibration decay. Operators compensate manually, inconsistently, and only after scrapping parts. The correction lives in a technician's head rather than in the system.
To equip manufacturers, motorsports teams, aerospace suppliers, maritime operators, and agricultural producers with scan-to-optimize manufacturing that improves accuracy, reduces cost, shortens timelines, and preserves legacy components that would otherwise be unrecoverable.
ScanIQLLC is a California limited liability company, with a Montana entity in formation to support planned 
operations in that state. As part of this program, the company will convert to a Delaware C-corporation — the standard structure for institutional investment and for federal SBIR participation. This conversion is budgeted and scheduled within the first program phase.Mission
 
The platform operates in two modes, both built on the same underlying engine:
•Replicate — dimensional fidelity. Faithful reproduction of legacy, discontinued, and obsolete 
components for which no digital model exists.
•Optimize — generative reformulation. Reformulated versions of a component with improved strength-
to-weight characteristics, produced within the same closed-loop verification cycle.
 
Across aerospace, marine, construction, agriculture, and motorsports, a large installed base of equipment depends on parts that are discontinued, out of production, or were never digitally modeled. Recovering such a part today requires manual reverse engineering: skilled labor, specialized measurement, and weeks of effort per component — assuming the expertise is available at all. For much of the installed base, it is not, and the equipment is retired early.
 
This is the structural failure. Manufacturing software issues instructions and never observes the outcome. There is no feedback path from the finished part back to the geometry that produced it. Consequently, every error is discovered after the fact and repeated on the next run. The result is scrapped material, extended timelines, and precision that depends on the operator rather than the system.

4. The Solution
 
5
ScanIQ closes theloopacross four stages:
Scan. A physical component is captured using LiDAR and photogrammetric methods, including consumer- grade capture hardware already in wide circulation.Optimize. The captured component is reconstructed as a continuous geometric field rather than a triangle mesh. This representation preserves fidelity through reconstruction, modification, and toolpath generation, and supports generative reformulation for strength-to-weight improvement.Print. The engine generates machine-ready code directly from the geometric field, calibrated to the individual machine. The architecture is machine-agnostic and applies to both additive and subtractive processes.Measure. The finished part is measured using optical sensors already onboard the production machine. Deviation from intended geometry is quantified and returned to the engine, which corrects the next iteration.The measurement stage is what distinguishes the platform. Competing tools address a single stage of this sequence. None observes the physical result and feeds it back. Our provisional patent covers the coupling of continuous field-based geometry representation with autonomous optical measurement feedback — a closed-loop, self-optimizing manufacturing system.Note on disclosure: this document intentionally omits implementation detail, toolchain composition, and algorithmic specifics. Technical diligence materials are available under a mutual non-disclosure agreement.
ScanIQ — Business Plan — Confidential
5. Three-Phase Market Strategy
 
6
Theplatform ishorizontal, but acompany at this stage cannot be. Our strategy sequences three markets 
deliberately: prove the loop where iteration is fast and parts are small, expand into markets where legacy replication carries the highest value, then enter agricultural and livestock applications where the underlying geometric capability opens a distinct research frontier.
 
 
Motocross and supercross are our beachhead for structural reasons, not sentimental ones. Parts are small, geometrically demanding, and high-value. Iteration cycles are measured in days because race weekends impose real deadlines. Failure is immediately visible — a component either performs under load or it does not. This is an ideal environment in which to stress a closed-loop system and accumulate calibration data quickly.Co-founder Jacqueline Anderson's established relationships across professional motocross and performance suspension give the company direct access to this market. Current pilot relationships include Stapes Performance, a Showa-authorized suspension operation, and MX6 Racing.
•Deploy the dealer platform to pilot shops on a paid subscription basis.•Process 100 parts through the full closed loop; publish dimensional repeatability data. •Complete Delaware C-corporation conversion.•Submit NSF SBIR Project Pitch and prepare the full proposal.
 
Aerospace and maritime operators maintain equipment whose components are frequently obsolete, long- lead, or entirely unavailable. In these sectors the cost of an unavailable part is not the part — it is the grounded aircraft or the vessel out of service. This is where Replicate mode carries its highest economic value, and where our founder's background in marine and submersible systems design is directly applicable.
•Convert enterprise discussions — Platinum Eagle Aerospace, FlexAI, and Oceanus Marine Technologies 
— into signed pilot agreements.
•Develop qualification-grade dimensional documentation suitable for regulated environments.

Phase 2 relocates operations to Montana and opens an agricultural track with two components.The near-term commercial component is legacy agricultural equipment restoration. Montana's cattle and ranching economy runs on equipment that is frequently decades old, with parts that are discontinued and suppliers that no longer exist. This is the same Replicate capability proven in Phases 1 and 2, applied to a market with acute and underserved need.The research component addresses lattice and biomimetic structures for animal science applications. Our engine's native capability to generate complex internal lattice geometry — structures that are impractical to model in conventional mesh-based CAD — is directly relevant to scaffold and structured-substrate work in animal reproductive science. We intend to pursue this through a formal research collaboration with Montana State University, whose College of Agriculture and Department of Animal & Range Sciences conduct research spanning nutrition, genetics, reproduction, and microbiology in animal agriculture, and which maintains R1 research classification and affiliation with USDA-ARS facilities including the Fort Keogh Livestock and Range Research Laboratory.Status and honest framing: the company has received expressions of interest from Montana agricultural contacts and has a planned relocation with established personal ties to the region's veterinary and equine community. We do not currently hold an executed research agreement. Securing one is a stated milestone and a prerequisite for any USDA SBIR submission; a $10,000 scoping study with Montana State University is budgeted within Phase 1 to begin that work. Applications in embryonic and reproductive technology are a research direction under investigation, not a present capability, and are represented as such throughout this document.

6. Market Analysis
 
 
7. Management Team
 
8
 
Deep expertise in construction operations, manufacturing, and logistics, with extensive experience in professional motocross — supporting race operations, technical coordination, and high-performance suspension development, an environment in which fractions of a second and micron-level precision determine outcomes. This background informs a focus on data-driven decision-making, quality control, and process improvement.
 
Full-stack systems engineer responsible for the design, construction, and deployment of the entire ScanIQ pipeline, including the multi-agent architecture, the geometry engine, and cloud infrastructure. Background spans biomimetic engineering, submersible and marine systems design through SubSurface Designs, and production automation systems. Directly responsible for the technical roadmap and federal proposal development.
 
Slicing software generates toolpaths but is open-loop and mesh-based; it never observes the finished part. Scan-to-CAD services and software are manual and expert-driven, producing a static file rather than a converging system. Generative design tools are capable on the design side but terminate at export, with no physical measurement feedback. Each addresses one stage. None owns the loop.Our defensibility rests on three elements: the patent-pending coupling of field representation with optical feedback; a machine-agnostic architecture that rides the installed sensor base rather than selling competing hardware; and a compounding data asset, in that every closed loop improves the calibration and geometry 
datasetunderlyingthe next.
The globaladditive manufacturing market is estimated at approximately $37.6 billion in 2026 and is projected 
to reach roughly $168.9 billion by 2033, a compound annual growth rate of approximately 23.9% (Grand View Research). Our addressable position sits in the software and intelligence layer of this market rather than in hardware or materials, which carries software economics: high gross margin and negligible marginal cost per additional part processed.
 
Three conditions have converged. First, modern production machines now ship with optical sensors — micro- lidar and cameras — as standard equipment, creating a large installed sensor base that is currently idle for measurement purposes. ScanIQ requires no new hardware to exploit it. Second, multi-agent AI orchestration matured from research demonstration to deployable infrastructure within the last two years, making the reasoning layer this architecture requires practical for the first time. Third, the industry is migrating from mesh-based to field-based geometry representation in advanced manufacturing; we are built field-native from inception, while incumbents must retrofit.

8. Operations Plan
 
Facility strategyPhase 1 leases approximately 3,000 square feet of shop and laboratory space in California rather than constructing a facility. This is a capital discipline decision. Constructing a 7,000–10,000 square foot facility would consume between 48% and 123% of this raise for a bare shell alone, before climate control, electrical provisioning, or laboratory fit-out; a finished facility of that scale is a multiple of the entire capital request. Leased space at this scale costs approximately 13% of the raise across the full program and is fully sufficient for the additive platforms, metrology bench, and compute infrastructure the Phase 1 milestones require.A larger owned facility is the centrepiece of the company's Montana plan and is addressed separately in Section 13. It is explicitly scoped to be financed with purpose-built rural development debt rather than equity. No portion of this Phase 1 raise constructs a building. Growth capital raised in this round is allocated to engineering and market validation.Milestone summary

Ourmachine selection reflects adeliberate engineering trade-off rather than brand preference. Sensor-rich 
commercial platforms provide the optical feedback hardware our system is designed to exploit, but impose vendor access controls that constrain custom toolpath execution. Open-firmware platforms impose no such constraints but carry fewer onboard sensors. We therefore operate both: sensor-rich machines for feedback validation, open machines for unrestricted engine development. Proving that corrections generalize across platforms is itself a validation requirement — a correction that only works on one printer is a calibration, not a system.

Registration with the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) is a prerequisite for all federal awards and is the single most time-critical action in this plan: it requires two to six weeks to process, costs nothing, and gates seven of the twelve opportunities tracked. A complete Phase 2 line-item budget, a twelve-item non-dilutive funding tracker, and the hiring and delegation schedule are maintained in the company's capital deployment workbook, available on request.
Phase 2 beginsas theMontana snow clearsin spring 2027 and representsa stepchange in scale: a 
$5,000,000 eighteen-month program funded by blended capital rather than a single equity round. Its components are equity, federal SBIR awards, and — critically — purpose-built rural development debt for the facility itself.
 
The Montana manufacturing laboratory will be financed with a USDA Business & Industry (B&I) Guaranteed Loan, not a residential mortgage product. This distinction is material. FHA lending is restricted to owner-occupied residential property and cannot lawfully finance a commercial manufacturing facility leased to an operating company. The USDA B&I program, by contrast, exists precisely for this purpose: it guarantees loans for the purchase and development of land, buildings, and associated infrastructure for commercial and industrial use in rural areas.The program fits the company's circumstances closely. Eligibility requires a location outside any city or town exceeding 50,000 inhabitants, which the intended Montana site satisfies. Loans are available up to $25,000,000 with a federal guarantee of up to 80%, materially improving both terms and approval probability relative to conventional commercial debt. Applications are accepted year-round through participating lenders. The program additionally offers reduced guarantee fees for locally owned and managed businesses supporting value-added agriculture — a category into which the company's agricultural manufacturing track falls directly.The property will be held by a separate ownership entity and leased to ScanIQ at arm's length. This is a conventional structure, but it requires careful construction: B&I regulations render ineligible any distribution or payment to a party retaining an ownership interest in the borrower. The lease-back arrangement will therefore be structured with counsel experienced in eligible-passive-company financing before any application is submitted. SBA 504 financing is retained as an alternative should the rural eligibility test or program terms prove unfavourable.No portion of the Phase 1 raise constructs this facility. Equity is reserved for engineering and validation; the building is financed with debt against the asset itself, at a fraction of the cost of equity.

14. Risk Factors and Mitigation
 
Key person risk
 
Partnership riskPhase 3 depends on securing a university research collaboration that is not yet executed, and USDA competitiveness depends materially on that collaboration. Mitigation: partnership execution is a gating milestone, budgeted and scheduled ahead of any USDA submission. Should the collaboration not materialize, Phase 3 proceeds on the agricultural equipment restoration track, which requires no research partner.
Concentration risk
 
Technicalvalidation risk
 
Platform dependency risk
 
18
Early revenuedepends on a small number of pilot relationships in a single vertical. Mitigation: the phased 
strategy deliberately diversifies into aerospace, maritime, and agricultural markets on a defined schedule rather than opportunistically.
Vendor firmwareaccesscontrols could restrict custom toolpath execution on sensor-rich commercial 
machines. Mitigation: the dual-platform strategy described in Section 8 ensures no critical development path depends on a single vendor's access policy.
Technicalcapability is presently concentrated in one founder. Mitigation: the first funded hire is an engineer 
specifically to distribute that capability, and documentation standards are budgeted within the program.
Ourdimensional results to date derive from a limited number of calibrated iterations. Repeatability across 
parts, materials, and machines is not yet statistically established. Mitigation: Phase 1 is explicitly structured to process 100 parts through the full loop and publish repeatability data, converting a promising result into a defensible claim before it is relied upon commercially or in federal proposals.
